summary: MMI said Thursday it raised $125 million in a Series D financing to expand access to its robotic microsurgery system in the U.S. as well as key global markets. The Symani robotic system is designed for soft tissue open surgery, allowing surgeons to repair tiny structures such as lymphatic vessels and nerves. The robot filters out tremors while translating the surgeon’s hand and wrist motions into robotic movement of its miniaturized instruments. MMI also plans to use the new funds to generate more clinical evidence for robotic microsurgery, including in the REMIND clinical trial evaluating the robot’s use in people with Alzheimer’s disease.
